item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Evaluation of the prognostic impact of germinal predisposition in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) (Univ. FIRENZE)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-16 23:59
Institution: Univ. FIRENZE, Milano
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-09 Malattie del sangue, oncologia e reumatologia

To identify conditions of genetic predisposition in hematologic neoplasias, and in particular in myelodysplastic syndromes, is a relevant clinical objective. It is not yet clear what is the prognostic impact of these predisposing mutations and which is the best tool to evaluate prognosis in their presence. The project here presented aims to verify the incidence and outcome of MDS patients with germinal predispositition.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Studio delle polineuropatie periferiche attraverso un approccio multimodale avanzato basato sull'integrazione di ecografia, elettromiografia e tecniche dedicate alla valutazione delle fibre nervose di piccolo calibro (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-16 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-12 Neurologia

The aim of this project is to investigate the involvement of large- and small-diameter nerve fibers through an innovative integrated approach. This approach combines the conventional assessment of large-diameter fibers using electromyography with ultrasound and advanced techniques for studying small-diameter fibers, including skin biopsy, laser-evoked potentials, and microneurography. The combined use of these techniques is the project’s original contribution. Since they are available at only a small number of centers nationally and internationally, their integration may improve diagnostic accuracy and enable earlier recognition of peripheral polyneuropathy. Testicular tumors are a heterogeneous group of neoplasms for which currently available biomarkers still show limited accuracy and sensitivity. Some miRNAs have demonstrated significant diagnostic potential in testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs); however, data on their expression profiles in serum and seminal plasma from patients with seminoma and non-germ cell tumors, such as Leydig cell tumors, are lacking. Colorectal carcinoma (CRC) frequently harbors mutations in tumor suppressor genes—including *TP53*—that are associated with tumor progression and treatment resistance. Mutant p53 (mutp53) has been shown to sustain HDAC6 expression, thereby promoting DNA damage repair and resistance to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress via ATF6. Preliminary data suggest that ATF6 increases TRAPPC4 expression, promoting the trafficking of PD-L1 to the cell membrane. Furthermore, HDAC6 deacetylates MSH2 and promotes its degradation, thereby impairing mismatch repair and contributing to mutation accumulation, neoantigen production, and immune checkpoint expression. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Molecular mechanisms of nephroprotection by SGLT2 inhibitors: interaction between SIRT1 and hypoxia signaling in diabetic nephropathy (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-07 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-08 Endocrinologia, nefrologia e scienze dell'alimentazione e del benessere

This project aims to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the nephroprotective effects of SGLT2 inhibition, with a focus on the role of the SIRT1/HIF-1α/HIF-2α signaling axis in diabetic nephropathy. The study will explore how empagliflozin (EMPA) modulates the balance between HIF-1α and HIF-2α through SIRT1 activation and how these pathways influence cellular adaptation to metabolic and hypoxic stress.
